title: Compiler errors, warnings, link errors and runtime failures
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or control flow.
Recognize common failure and safety cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Build failures occur at different stages. Syntax and constraint violations are diagnosed during translation; unresolved external symbols may appear at link time; runtime failures occur after a program starts. Warnings identify suspicious code that may still compile.
understand.whyItMatters: Identifying the failure stage narrows investigation and avoids changing unrelated code. A successful compile does not prove runtime correctness.
understand.analogy: Treat each resource and operation as having a clear contract, valid lifetime and failure path.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, compiler or library specifications.

explain.narrative:
Build failures occur at different stages. Syntax and constraint violations are diagnosed during translation; unresolved external symbols may appear at link time; runtime failures occur after a program starts. Warnings identify suspicious code that may still compile.

Check object bounds, lifetimes, arithmetic limits and all relevant return values. Compile with warnings enabled and test both normal and failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: This minimal program can be compiled, linked and run as separate stages by many toolchains. Each stage has different inputs and possible diagnostics.

practise.guidedTask: Classify sample messages as compile-time, link-time or runtime failures.
practise.independentTask: Intentionally create one syntax error, one missing definition and one runtime failure. Record how each tool reports it.
hints: Read the first relevant diagnostic and inspect the source location before changing code.
A warning is not necessarily a build failure, but it should be understood and resolved where possible.
Runtime tests do not replace compile-time diagnostics.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to protect correctness?
options: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
Ignore the type and lifetime rules.
questions.answer: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
questions.explanation: C requires explicit handling of object validity and operation failures.

questions.prompt: How should the example be checked?
options: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
Ignore diagnostics and test only once.
questions.answer: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
questions.explanation: Warnings and targeted tests provide evidence for correctness.
